**q < 570**, improving the previous analytic cutoff of 2,000.

[Read the fifteen-page proof](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/releases/download/v0.6.0/tenth-discriminant-v0.6.0.pdf) · [Download the proof and verification bundle](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/releases/download/v0.6.0/tenth-discriminant-v0.6.0.zip) · [Source and reproduction](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/tree/v0.6.0/versions/v6)

This contribution to Terence Tao's tenth-discriminant challenge retains
the smoothed prime sum from the exact determinant valuation, feeds it
into the factorial bounds through eight acyclic refinements, and combines
stronger residual Frobenius divisibility with joint derivative/radius
estimates. An auxiliary inert prime supplies the monomial width, while a
positive squared-polynomial kernel sharpens the comparison with the
quadratic norm series. All approximation errors are explicit.

The new argument excludes the whole real interval `[570,2,000]`; the
[audited v5 result](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/releases/tag/v0.5.0)
supplies `q >= 2,000`. The new interval is treated in full relative to the
stated classical inputs, with no dependency on intermediate unpublished
drafts. No quasi-Riemann hypothesis, quadratic zero-free theorem,
quartic-field determinant, or Masser theorem is used.

The paper builds on Green's derivative determinant, van Dijk's
auxiliary-prime rank argument, and norm-counting and disk ideas from the
challenge discussion. The
[research and attribution record](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/v0.6.0/versions/v6/RESEARCH.md)
identifies those contributions and describes tested alternatives.

The certificates pass 429 grouped exact rational checks, including
1,258 interval cells, with a smallest certified gap greater than
`0.010389`. A complete isolated rerun reproduces all exact band outputs
and refinement stages. A further 101,524 finite structural cases pass;
the finite scan checks 70 candidates below 570 and verifies the nine
surviving discriminants.

**Independent mathematical audit of v6 is pending.** Earlier audits do
not cover it, and these checks are not formal verification. Codex
developed the refinements, manuscript, and verification programs. See
the [review record](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/v0.6.0/versions/v6/REVIEW.md)
for scope and audit targets. The cutoff is a practical stopping point
for this research pass, not an optimality theorem.

This is a research prerelease. All earlier version files, tags, and
release assets are preserved.
